requirements.title: Straight-key closure to key-down
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall hold its key-down output asserted for the whole of each debounced straight-key closure in Straight mode.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-038 (SI-018 core requirement, one requirement per key type; ADR-009): the straight key is manually timed, so the keyer passes the debounced contact state through as key-down. The contact state arrives across ICD-CTL-SW from the key inputs of ICD-CTL-KEY (tip is the straight key by default, CON-012). The manual-closure timeout REQ-SW-KEYER-026 bounds a held contact. Ops: OPS-005.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): debounced closures of 1 ms to 4 s, key-down compared with the contact state sample by sample. Post-build (supporting): Bench logic capture of the tip contact and the keyer test point in TC-SYS-026. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-001.

requirements.title: Straight-mode input selection
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall key Straight mode from the tip, the ring or either contact as the operator's Straight-input setting selects.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-038; ADR-009 decides Straight on tip by default with ring and both options. With the tip setting the ring is ignored, which makes a mono (TS) plug that grounds the ring harmless (HZ-004 K2, cause C1). Ops: OPS-005, OPS-013. Depends on: REQ-SYS-174 (key jack wiring: tip, ring, sleeve) and REQ-SYS-047 (contact thresholds) in hardware; the operator selects the tip setting for a mono plug (OPS-013). Fault tolerance: docs/safety/hazard-analysis.md 8.1 item 4.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): each setting with tip, ring and both contacts closed in turn, including the ring held closed for 10 s in the tip setting; key-down follows only the selected contacts. Post-build (supporting): Bench with a TS plug in TC-SYS-037. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-002.

requirements.title: Self-completing paddle elements
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall complete every started paddle element to its full nominal length whatever the paddle state after it starts.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-039 (SI-018 iambic paddles with a built-in keyer; ADR-009). Self-completing elements are part of the Curtis 8044 keyer semantics that docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F7 item 2 encodes; golden vectors V1 and V2 check them. Ops: OPS-004.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): vectors V1 and V2 of docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F7 at 5, 20 and 50 WPM, paddle released 1 ms after closure. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-003.

requirements.title: Non-shortening inter-element space
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall follow every paddle element with a one-dit inter-element space that no paddle closure shortens.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-039; Curtis 8044: the space between elements is never allowed to shorten by early key closure (docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F7 item 2). Golden vectors V3 and V11 check it; V12 checks that a same-paddle tap during an element is ignored. Ops: OPS-004.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): vectors V3, V11 and V12 of docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F7 at 5, 20 and 50 WPM, with closures injected at every 1 ms sample of the space. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-004.

requirements.title: Dot and dash memory
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall send the opposite element after the current element and space when the opposite paddle closes during either.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-039. Curtis 8044: dot memory is essential in any serious electronic keyer and true iambic operation needs both dot and dash memories (docs/research/keyer-and-key-interfaces.md F3; docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F7 item 3). Golden vectors V4 (fast N) and V5 (fast A) check it. Ops: OPS-004.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): vectors V4 and V5 of docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F7 in Iambic A and Iambic B at 5, 20 and 50 WPM. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-005.

requirements.title: Squeeze alternation
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall send alternating dits and dahs, starting with the first-closed paddle's element, while both paddles stay closed in Iambic A and B.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-040 (keyer modes, NGO-013). WinKeyer3: in either iambic mode, alternating dits and dahs are sent while both paddles are held closed (docs/research/keyer-and-key-interfaces.md F3); a simultaneous first closure starts with a dit (docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F7 item 1). Golden vector V10 checks it. Ops: OPS-004.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): vector V10 of docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F7 and simultaneous-closure variants, in Iambic A and Iambic B at 5, 20 and 50 WPM. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-006.

requirements.title: Iambic A squeeze release
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall, in Iambic A mode, send no further element after the one in progress when both paddles open during a squeeze.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-040. Curtis mode A: when a squeeze is released, the element underway is completed and nothing else follows (docs/research/keyer-and-key-interfaces.md F3; docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F7 item 4, no squeeze latch in mode A). Iambic A is the proposed default (REQ-SYS-136; D-KN1, Proposed, owner decision pending at SRR). Golden vectors V6, V7 and V8 in mode A check it. Ops: OPS-004.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): vectors V6, V7 and V8 of docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F7 in Iambic A at 5, 20 and 50 WPM. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-007.

requirements.title: Iambic B squeeze release
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall, in Iambic B mode, send one alternate element after a squeeze held past the switchpoint of the element in progress.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-040. Curtis mode B: a squeeze released during an element causes another alternate element to follow it (docs/research/keyer-and-key-interfaces.md F3). The switchpoint is the fraction of the element after which a held squeeze latches the alternate element (docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F7 item 4; 0 is pure Curtis B). Golden vectors V6, V7, V8, V9, V9b and V13 check it. Ops: OPS-004.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): vectors V6, V7, V8, V9, V9b and V13 of docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F7 in Iambic B with switchpoints 0 and 50 percent at 5, 20 and 50 WPM. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-008.

requirements.title: Iambic B switchpoint range
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall accept Iambic B switchpoint settings from 0 to 90 percent of the element length in 10 percent steps (TBR).
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-040; the switchpoint decides how early a squeeze latches in mode B, and a wrong value makes paddle feel unpleasant (RSK-012; docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F7 and F14: 0 to 90 percent, default 50 percent, a Proposal). The 10 percent step is this author's proposal. Ops: OPS-004. TBR: range, step and the default are set by the owner's human-in-the-loop session (RSK-012 mitigation S3).
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): every setting from 0 to 90 percent accepted and applied to vector V9, and 95 and 100 percent rejected with the previous setting kept. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-009.

tbr.owner: Robin decides at SRR on Claude's proposal; Claude produces the closing evidence
tbr.plan: The owner's human-in-the-loop session on the Pico 2 development board before PDR (RSK-012 mitigation S3, credit false) fixes the range, step and default; Robin approves them in the PDR decision memo.

requirements.title: Ultimatic squeeze
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall, in Ultimatic mode, repeat the element of the last-closed paddle while both paddles stay closed.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-040 (Ultimatic is one of the five modes of NGO-013; D-KN1, Proposed, owner decision pending at SRR). WinKeyer3: in Ultimatic mode, when both paddles are pressed the keyer sends a continuous stream of whichever paddle was last pressed (docs/research/keyer-and-key-interfaces.md F3). Ops: OPS-004.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): dit then dah, and dah then dit, held together for 1 s at 5, 20 and 50 WPM; release of either paddle returns to the other's element. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-010.

requirements.title: Bug-mode dits
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall, in Bug mode, generate self-timed dits with one-dit spaces while the dit contact stays closed.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-040 (Bug is one of the five modes of NGO-013). WinKeyer3 Bug mode sends the dits while the operator sends the dahs manually (docs/research/keyer-and-key-interfaces.md F3). Ops: OPS-004.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): dit contact held 1 s at 5, 20 and 50 WPM; dit count and spacing compared with the nominal. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-011.

requirements.title: Bug-mode manual dah
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall, in Bug mode, hold key-down for the whole of each debounced dah-contact closure.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-040: in Bug mode the dah is manually timed (docs/research/keyer-and-key-interfaces.md F3), so the dah contact is a manually timed contact bounded by the manual-closure timeout REQ-SW-KEYER-026 (HZ-004 K3). Ops: OPS-004.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): dah closures of 1 ms to 4 s, key-down compared with the debounced contact sample by sample. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-012.

requirements.title: Element and space timing
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall time each generated dit, dah and inter-element space within +/-0.5 percent or +/-0.2 ms of nominal, whichever is larger.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-042. Nominal: dit 1200/WPM ms, dah 3 dits, inter-element space 1 dit (ITU-R M.1677-1 section 2, PARIS; docs/research/keyer-and-key-interfaces.md F4). The tolerance is the MOP-012 target, tighter than the parent's threshold so that the hardware path keeps margin (02 section 4.6); the 0.2 ms floor is two steps of the 100 us HostUnit clock (docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F8). Ops: OPS-004.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): PARIS strings and vectors V1 to V13 at 5, 15, 25 and 50 WPM. Post-build (supporting): Bench, keyer test point in TC-SYS-028. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-013.

requirements.title: Timing under display and encoder load on the target
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall hold element and space errors within +/-0.5 percent or +/-0.2 ms at 50 display frames/s and 50 detents/s per encoder (TBR).
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-042: host timing does not show interrupt and task contention on the RP2350, and user-interface latency causes wrongly timed elements (docs/research/keyer-and-key-interfaces.md section 4.2 item 20 and R4; RSK-012 mitigation S6), so element timing is confirmed on the target under a stated load. 50 frames/s is one full frame per 20 ms, the memory LCD update of docs/research/display-and-ui-parts.md candidate UI-DSP-01; 50 detents/s per encoder exceeds 2 revolutions/s of a 24-detent encoder (ADR-006). Target timing closes at Bench, never by Emulation (CON-025). Ops: OPS-004. KDR: rustos timer and alarm work package WP-SW-01. TBR: load values pending the PDR display and encoder design.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (supporting): HostUnit with a scheduler load model; Bench on the Pico 2 development board with credit false. Post-build (closing): Bench on the delivered unit (credit row T-SW-TARGET), Pico-based logic capture at 1 MS/s of the keyer test point for PARIS at 5, 25 and 50 WPM while a fixture turns both encoders at 50 detents/s each and the display pushes a full frame every 20 ms. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-014.

tbr.owner: Robin decides at SRR on Claude's proposal; Claude produces the closing evidence
tbr.plan: The PDR display driver and encoder decode design confirms the 20 ms full-frame time and the 50 detents/s decode rate; Robin approves the load values in the PDR decision memo.

requirements.title: Keyer speed setting range
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall accept keyer speed settings from 5 to 50 WPM in 1 WPM steps.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-041; SI-033 and ADR-024 accept 5 to 50 WPM, and NGO-013 sets 1 WPM steps; 5 WPM lets beginner friends operate (SI-019). Ops: OPS-004.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): every setting from 5 to 50 WPM accepted and timed, 4 and 51 WPM rejected with the previous setting kept. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-015.

requirements.title: Speed change at the element boundary
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall apply a speed change from the next element, leaving the element and space in progress at their starting lengths.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-041; ADR-024 section 4.3 asks that a speed change while sending does not truncate the element in progress, because the speed control is adjustable while sending (ADR-024 section 4.1). Ops: OPS-004.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): speed changed at every 1 ms sample of a dah and of the following space, between 5 and 50 WPM in both directions. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-016.

requirements.title: Paddle-to-element latency
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall start a paddle-initiated element from idle within 2 ms (TBR) of the first input sample that reads the paddle closed.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-043 (3 ms from the contact): up to 1 ms falls before the first 1 ms sample, leaving 2 ms for the make filter and the element start (docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F8; the MOP-012 latency target is 2 ms). Ops: OPS-004. TBR: follows the make-filter value of REQ-SYS-048.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): 50 closures from idle at random phases of the sample clock at 15 and 50 WPM. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-017.

tbr.owner: Robin decides at SRR on Claude's proposal; Claude produces the closing evidence
tbr.plan: Closes with REQ-SYS-048: Claude captures the owner's key and paddle bounce before PDR and Robin approves the make-filter value, which fixes this latency, in the PDR decision memo.

requirements.title: Straight-key closure latency
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall assert key-down within 2 ms (TBR) of the first input sample that reads the straight-key contact closed.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-160 (15 ms contact to RF rise, of which at most 12 ms is the lead-in of REQ-SYS-161 and the rest is sampling and debounce; ADR-010). 2 ms plus up to 1 ms before the first sample fits the 3 ms debounce share of the parent. Ops: OPS-005. TBR: follows the make-filter value of REQ-SYS-048.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): 50 straight-key closures at random phases of the sample clock. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-018.

tbr.owner: Robin decides at SRR on Claude's proposal; Claude produces the closing evidence
tbr.plan: Closes with REQ-SYS-048 and REQ-SYS-160: the bounce capture and the T/R element trade at PDR fix the value; Robin approves it in the PDR decision memo.

requirements.title: Key input sampling period
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall sample both key inputs every 1.000 ms +/-0.010 ms.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-043, whose 3 ms latency budget assumes 1 ms sampling, and HZ-004 K9 and HZ-010 K3 (debounce at a 1 kHz sample rate; ADR-009 section 2). +/-0.010 ms is ten ticks of the 1 us TIMER0 (docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F14: sampling from TIMER0 ALARM1). REQ-SYS-051 and REQ-SYS-054 have no SW-KEYER child: the CTL input network holds RF immunity (HZ-010 K2, K4), with this sampling and the debounce as firmware margin, and the safe-state manager runs the paddle watchdog (HZ-004 K4; 07 section 14.1). Ops: OPS-004, OPS-005, OPS-017. Depends on: REQ-SYS-047 and REQ-SYS-051 (the key input network sets the levels and RF immunity the samples read). Fault tolerance: docs/safety/hazard-analysis.md 8.1 item 4.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (supporting): HostUnit of the sampling schedule on the simulated clock. Post-build (closing): Bench on the delivered unit (credit row T-SW-TARGET), instrumented build that toggles a test pad at each sample, Pico-based logic capture at 1 MS/s for 10 s while keying at 50 WPM. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-019.

requirements.title: Key closure debounce
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall accept a key-input closure only after 2 consecutive 1 ms samples (TBR) read the input closed.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-048; bounce of unknown keys must not add or drop elements (MOE-005; HZ-010 K3, HZ-004 K9; docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F6, F14, Proposal). Convention: N consecutive 1 ms samples accept every contact of N ms or more and reject every contact shorter than N-1 ms. The count is fixed, not operator-configurable (Proposed, owner decision pending at SRR): a make filter above 2 samples leaves no time inside the 2 ms of REQ-SW-KEYER-017, so the 1 to 20 ms range of HZ-004 K9 is not adopted. Ops: OPS-004, OPS-005, OPS-017. Depends on: REQ-SYS-047 and REQ-SYS-051 (input levels and RF immunity). Fault tolerance: docs/safety/hazard-analysis.md 8.1 item 4. TBR: stands until the owner's key and paddle bounce is captured.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): debounce vectors D1 to D5 of docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F6 and recorded bounce patterns of 0.1 to 10 ms, on each input. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-020.

tbr.owner: Robin decides at SRR on Claude's proposal; Claude produces the closing evidence
tbr.plan: Closes with REQ-SYS-048: Claude captures the owner's key and paddle bounce with the Pico-based logic capture before PDR (A-KN5); Robin approves the value in the PDR decision memo.

requirements.title: Key opening debounce
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall accept a key-input opening only after 5 consecutive 1 ms samples (TBR) read the input open.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-162; the slower break filter absorbs bounce so no element is added (MOE-005; HZ-010 K3, HZ-004 K9; docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F6, F14, Proposal). Convention: N consecutive 1 ms samples accept every break of N ms or more and reject any shorter than N-1 ms. The count is fixed at 6 samples or fewer (25 percent of a 50 WPM dit), not operator-configurable (Proposed, owner decision pending at SRR): a longer filter lengthens every manual element, so the 1 to 20 ms range of HZ-004 K9 is not adopted. Ops: OPS-004, OPS-005, OPS-017. Depends on: REQ-SYS-047 and REQ-SYS-051 (input levels and RF immunity). Fault tolerance: docs/safety/hazard-analysis.md 8.1 item 4. TBR: stands until the owner's key and paddle bounce is captured.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): debounce vectors D1 to D5 of docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F6 and recorded break-bounce patterns of 0.1 to 10 ms, on each input. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-021.

tbr.owner: Robin decides at SRR on Claude's proposal; Claude produces the closing evidence
tbr.plan: Closes with REQ-SYS-162: the bounce capture before PDR (A-KN5) sets the value; Robin approves it in the PDR decision memo.

requirements.title: Key-closed interlock
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall withhold key-down after boot, reset or mode change until each input the mode uses reads open for 500 consecutive samples (TBR).
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-052; HZ-004 K1 and HZ-014 K6: a stuck paddle, a held key or a mono plug at switch-on never keys (NGO-021, MOE-012; ADR-009). Only the inputs the mode uses are checked (REQ-SYS-163). The samples are those of REQ-SW-KEYER-019; any closed sample restarts the count, so the check repeats every sample (HZ-004 K1). Ops: OPS-013, OPS-021. Depends on: REQ-SYS-119 (pull-downs hold TX off during reset), REQ-SYS-055 (hardware cutoff) and REQ-TX-014 (no RF with TX_KEY idle); the operator removes the plug or selects Straight on tip (OPS-013). Fault tolerance: docs/safety/hazard-analysis.md 8.1 item 4. TBR: interlock time pending the F13 decision.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): inputs closed at boot, after a simulated reset and after each mode change, for 0 to 2 s in 10 ms steps; key-down stays idle until 500 consecutive open samples. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-022.

tbr.owner: Robin decides at SRR on Claude's proposal; Claude produces the closing evidence
tbr.plan: Closes with REQ-SYS-052: Robin decides the interlock at SRR; the HostUnit bounce study at PDR confirms 500 ms.

requirements.title: KEY inhibit report
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall report each KEY inhibit onset and its cause to the display interface within 20 ms.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-067 (distinct fault cause message within 1 s). docs/conops/conops.md Table 3.4-4 names the keyer's two KEY inhibit causes: row 1, the key-closed interlock of REQ-SW-KEYER-022 ('KEY CLOSED: check plug', HZ-004 K1), and row 2, the manual-closure timeout of REQ-SW-KEYER-026 ('KEY?', HZ-004 K3); row 3, the paddle watchdog, belongs to the safe-state manager (HZ-004 K4). 20 ms leaves the rest of the 1 s to the display task and the memory LCD refresh; this author's proposal. Ops: OPS-013. Depends on: the operator reads the message and removes the plug, opens the contact or changes the mode (OPS-013). Fault tolerance: docs/safety/hazard-analysis.md 8.1 item 4.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): each interlock entry path (boot, reset, mode change) and each manual-closure timeout (Straight tip, ring and both; Bug-mode dah contact) with a mock display interface, cause and report time measured on the simulated clock. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-023.

requirements.title: Key-input mode change by menu only
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall change its key-input mode only on a mode-selection command from the menu.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-056; HZ-004 K2 and D-KN8 (Proposed, owner decision pending at SRR): no automatic key-type detection in revision A (ADR-009 alternative D deferred), so plug insertion never changes the mode. 07 section 14.2 row (d) adds a separate confirmation before the menu issues the command (SWE-134 d), while HZ-004 K2 and REQ-SYS-056 name the menu selection only; under either the keyer changes mode only on the command. Ops: OPS-013. Depends on: REQ-SYS-174 (jack wiring) and the operator's menu selection (OPS-013). Fault tolerance: docs/safety/hazard-analysis.md 8.1 item 4 (SWE-134 d).
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): plug insertion and removal, jack-detect changes, every input pattern, resets and configuration reloads leave the mode unchanged; only the mode-selection command changes it. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-024.

requirements.title: Mode selection with a closed input
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall accept a key-input mode-selection command while any key input reads closed.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-163: a mono (TS) plug grounds the ring permanently, so without this the Straight-on-tip selection could never be made with the plug in (HZ-004 K2). Transmit stays disarmed until the inputs the new mode uses pass the interlock REQ-SW-KEYER-022. Ops: OPS-013, OPS-005. Depends on: the operator's menu selection (OPS-013). Fault tolerance: docs/safety/hazard-analysis.md 8.1 item 4 (SWE-134 d).
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): selection commands with the tip, the ring and both inputs closed, in every mode. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-025.

requirements.title: Manual-closure timeout
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall force key-down idle after 5 s (TBR) of continuous confirmed closure of a manually timed contact, until it reads open.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-053; HZ-004 K3 (with HZ-001 K3, HZ-003 K3, HZ-006 K6, HZ-012 K2): a held or shorted straight-key contact, or Bug-mode dah contact, ends within 5 s, 2.5 s below the 7.5 s floor of the hardware cutoff so that firmware acts first (NGO-021, MOE-012; D-KN3, Proposed, owner decision pending at SRR). Ops: OPS-013. Depends on: REQ-SYS-055 (independent hardware cutoff) and REQ-TX-014 in hardware; the operator opens the contact to re-arm (OPS-013). Fault tolerance: docs/safety/hazard-analysis.md 8.1 item 4. TBR: value pending D-KN3.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): Straight mode on tip, ring and both, and the Bug-mode dah contact, held 4.9, 5.0, 5.1 and 60 s; key-down idle from 5 s until the contact opens and re-arms after the opening debounce. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-026.

tbr.owner: Robin decides at SRR on Claude's proposal; Claude produces the closing evidence
tbr.plan: Closes with REQ-SYS-053: Robin decides D-KN3 at SRR; the configurable range (2 to 6 s) is fixed with it.

requirements.title: Sidetone during a manual-closure timeout
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall keep the sidetone gate asserted while a timed-out manually timed contact stays closed.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-053; HZ-004 K3 keeps the sidetone on during the timeout so that the operator hears the fault and opens the contact. Ops: OPS-013. Depends on: the operator hears the tone and opens the contact (OPS-013); REQ-SYS-071 bounds the headphone level in hardware. Fault tolerance: docs/safety/hazard-analysis.md 8.1 item 4.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): held contacts of REQ-SW-KEYER-026 past the timeout, sidetone gate state recorded each 1 ms sample. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-027.

requirements.title: Keying sources
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall assert key-down only from debounced key-input states or the running confirmed bench test-mode generator.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-007: 47 CFR 97.109(d) admits automatic control only for stations Part 97 designates, such as beacons under 97.203, so every element comes from the operator's key (CON-006). Revision A has no message memory or automatic identification, so the 20 WPM limit of 97.119(b)(1) never applies (CON-005). HZ-004 K13 covers the test mode. Ops: OPS-004, OPS-012. Depends on: REQ-SYS-179 (two-action test-mode entry) and REQ-TX-014 (no RF with TX_KEY idle). Fault tolerance: docs/safety/hazard-analysis.md 8.1 item 4 (no single software event starts a keying source).
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): 10 min of simulated operation in every mode with the inputs open and every menu, tune and configuration event injected; key-down asserts only from input closures or the confirmed generator. Inspection of the keying call graph is supporting. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-028.

requirements.title: Test-mode generator start
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall start its test-mode PARIS generator only on a confirmed bench-test-mode command.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-179 (bench test mode entered only after a menu selection and a separate confirmation; HZ-004 K13, SWE-134 d). The generator is the only keying source other than the key jack (REQ-SYS-007). Ops: OPS-012. Depends on: REQ-SYS-055 (hardware cutoff) in hardware; the operator's two separate actions (OPS-012). Fault tolerance: docs/safety/hazard-analysis.md 8.1 item 4.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): every command sequence without the confirmation, including a selection followed by a reset, leaves the generator stopped; the confirmed command starts it. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-029.

requirements.title: Key-down state integrity
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall force key-down idle within 1 ms when its key-down state and its stored complement disagree.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-120; HZ-004 K8 stores the keying state with its bitwise complement and checks it before every use, so a corrupted flag cannot key the transmitter (SWE-134 f and i; cause C7). Ops: OPS-021. Depends on: REQ-TX-014 and REQ-TX-003 (RF needs both TX_KEY and PA_EN in hardware). Fault tolerance: docs/safety/hazard-analysis.md 8.1 items 2 and 4. Constraint: the complement check is the method HZ-004 K8 names.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): fault injection flipping each bit of the key-down state and of its complement in every keyer state; key-down idle within 1 ms each time. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-030.

requirements.title: Key-up on keyer error or safe-state command
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall force key-down idle within 1 ms of a keyer error or a safe-state command.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-130 (PA off, key up and audio muted before any other action after a reset, panic or fault; HZ-004 K7; 07 section 14.2, SW-KEYER items c, k and l). Ops: OPS-021. Depends on: REQ-SYS-055 and REQ-SYS-119 (hardware bounds when firmware stops). Fault tolerance: docs/safety/hazard-analysis.md 8.1 item 4.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): every keyer error variant and a safe-state command injected in every keyer state and element phase. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-031.

requirements.title: Semi break-in hang
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall signal end of over after an operator-set hang of 3 to 30 dits (TBR) of the displayed speed from last key-up.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-044; SI-036, CON-021 and ADR-010 fix semi break-in with an adjustable hang (ADR-010 section 4.1 allocates the hang to SW-KEYER). The hang counts in dits of the displayed speed in every mode, Straight included (docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F11). Ops: OPS-004, OPS-005. TBR: range pending D-KN4.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): hang settings 3, 8 and 30 dits at 5, 15 and 50 WPM in Straight and Iambic A, end-of-over signal time measured from the last key-up. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-032.

tbr.plan: Closes with REQ-SYS-044: Robin decides D-KN4 at SRR; the sequencer timing table at PDR confirms the floor against relay timing.

requirements.title: Sidetone gate onset
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall assert the sidetone gate within 1 ms of each key-down assertion.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-159 (sidetone within 4 ms of the closure that starts an element); HZ-005 K4 sets sidetone onset within 1 ms of key-down (docs/research/keyer-verification-and-key-input-network.md F11, F14). Ops: OPS-004, OPS-005. Depends on: REQ-SYS-071 (headphone output ceiling) in hardware; the operator keys with headphones on (OPS-004). Fault tolerance: docs/safety/hazard-analysis.md 8.1 item 7 (Test).
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): key-down assertions in every mode, sidetone gate edge measured on the simulated clock. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-033.

requirements.title: Paddle memory integrity
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall force key-down idle and clear both paddle memories within 1 ms when a paddle memory and its stored complement disagree.
requirements.rationale: Self-derived: 07 section 14.2 SW-KEYER row item (f) (SWE-134 f) stores the dit and dah memories with their complements, as HZ-004 K8 does for the key-down state (REQ-SW-KEYER-030); a corrupted memory would otherwise send an element the operator did not key. Clearing both memories and forcing key-up is the known safe state; 1 ms matches REQ-SW-KEYER-030. Robin's concurrence is pending in the V2 record (02 section 2.3). Ops: OPS-021. Depends on: REQ-TX-014 and REQ-TX-003 (RF needs both TX_KEY and PA_EN in hardware). Fault tolerance: docs/safety/hazard-analysis.md 8.1 items 2 and 4.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): fault injection flipping each bit of the dit memory, the dah memory and each complement in every keyer state, memories set and clear; key-down idle and both memories clear within 1 ms each time. Post-build (closing): Bench on the delivered unit with the fault-injection build (credit row T-SW-TARGET, SWE-192). Closing cases: TC-SW-KEYER-041, TC-SW-KEYER-038.

requirements.title: Sidetone off during the key-closed interlock
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall hold the sidetone gate deasserted while the key-closed interlock of REQ-SW-KEYER-022 withholds key-down.
requirements.rationale: Self-derived: HZ-004 K1 and docs/conops/conops.md OPS-013 step 1 keep the sidetone off while the KEY inhibit of the interlock holds (Table 3.4-4 row 1), so a closed input at switch-on or reset makes no tone that reads as keying; REQ-SW-KEYER-027 is the opposite case, where the tone reports a contact stuck during use. REQ-SYS-052 covers transmit only. Robin's concurrence is pending in the V2 record (02 section 2.3). Ops: OPS-013, OPS-021. Depends on: the operator reads the KEY CLOSED message (REQ-SW-KEYER-023) and removes the plug or changes the mode (OPS-013). Fault tolerance: docs/safety/hazard-analysis.md 8.1 item 4.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): inputs closed across boot, a simulated reset and each mode change for 0 to 2 s, sidetone gate recorded every 1 ms sample until the interlock passes. Post-build (closing): Bench on the delivered unit (credit row T-SW-TARGET, SWE-192). Closing cases: TC-SW-KEYER-042, TC-SW-KEYER-034.

requirements.title: Key input closed without a plug
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall withhold key-down while any key input reads closed and the plug-presence input reads no plug (TBR).
requirements.rationale: Self-derived: 07 section 14.2 SW-KEYER row item (g) (SWE-134 g) asks for jack-detect range checks; a contact that reads closed with no plug in the jack is a shorted input network or pad, not an operator closure (HZ-004 K9, HZ-010), so it never keys. The other stuck-input checks of item (g) are REQ-SW-KEYER-022, REQ-SW-KEYER-026 and the safe-state manager's paddle watchdog (HZ-004 K4). Robin's concurrence is pending in the V2 record (02 section 2.3). Ops: OPS-013. Depends on: the plug-presence switch of ICD-CTL-KEY section 3.2.5 and REQ-SYS-055 (hardware cutoff). Fault tolerance: docs/safety/hazard-analysis.md 8.1 item 4. TBR: the plug-presence circuit is Preliminary in ICD-CTL-KEY. Hazard controls implemented (docs/safety/hazards.json control_req_ids): HZ-004 K9; HZ-010 K3.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): every mode with the mock plug-presence input reading no plug and the tip, the ring and both reading closed for 10 ms to 10 s; key-down stays idle; with the plug present the same closures key as the mode defines. Post-build (closing): Bench on the delivered unit (credit row T-SW-TARGET, SWE-192). Closing cases: TC-SW-KEYER-043, TC-SW-KEYER-034.

tbr.owner: Claude (ICD-CTL-KEY author) proposes; Robin approves in the PDR decision memo
tbr.plan: The CTL schematic at PDR confirms the plug-presence switch and its reading against the jack drawing (ICD-CTL-KEY TBR row for the plug-detect wiring); if the circuit is dropped, this requirement is retired by CR.

requirements.title: Out-of-range keyer setting commands
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall reject a speed, switchpoint or hang setting command outside its stated range and keep the previous setting.
requirements.rationale: Why: allocated from REQ-SYS-041, and from REQ-SYS-040 and REQ-SYS-044 for the switchpoint and the hang: an out-of-range command is the undesired event of these settings, and keeping the previous value leaves the keyer in a tested state. The ranges are those of REQ-SW-KEYER-015 (5 to 50 WPM), REQ-SW-KEYER-009 (0 to 90 percent in 10 percent steps) and REQ-SW-KEYER-032 (3 to 30 dits). Ops: OPS-004.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): the rejection steps of the speed, switchpoint and hang cases: values below, above and between the stated steps and the largest value of the command type, each rejected with the previous setting kept. Closing cases: TC-SW-KEYER-009, TC-SW-KEYER-015, TC-SW-KEYER-032.

requirements.title: Key inputs change no setting
requirements.description: The keyer firmware shall leave its speed, switchpoint, hang and Straight-input settings unchanged by every key-input pattern.
requirements.rationale: Self-derived: the key line is the command-injection surface of 07 section 16.2 row 'Keying and control inputs'; coding rule CS-30 and the ICD-CTL-KEY section 3.2.5 security row accept no key-line pattern as a command, and ADR-009 keeps every key setting on the menu. The key-input mode is REQ-SW-KEYER-024. Robin's concurrence is pending in the V2 record (02 section 2.3). Ops: OPS-004, OPS-017.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (closing): HostUnit, the cwht-core keyer on the host against cwht-hal-mock key inputs with the simulated microsecond clock stepped at 100 us (credit row T-SW-LOGIC; the keyer logic sits behind the HAL traits with time from the mock clock, so host execution is representative): the key-line flood, sub-filter glitches and crafted patterns of the cybersecurity case in every mode, every setting read back before and after. Closing case: TC-SW-KEYER-040.
